text:
Tess (Support): Hey team, customer using our streaming API with EventSource on Safari 16/17 seeing repeated disconnects and partial outputs. They claim sometimes only the first few events arrive, then connection closes with a 304 from their CDN. They pasted headers and say it works in Chrome. Need triage.
Ivy (Client Success): Customer is on CloudFront in front of our private deployment. They reported flaky behavior after they enabled caching rules to reduce bandwidth. They also mentioned they use an EventSource polyfill for older Safari.
Jun (Backend): Thanks. Can you paste the sample request/response headers? main suspects: caching/ETag, content-encoding buffering, or CDN converting to 304 and closing stream. Also needs proper SSE headers: `Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8`, `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform`, `Connection: keep-alive` and chunked transfer.
Tess (Support): Paste from customer:
```
GET /v1/streams/abc
Host: api.redwood.example
Accept: text/event-stream

Response:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/event-stream
cache-control: max-age=0
etag: "abc123"
content-encoding: gzip
content-length: 0
x-cache: Hit from cloudfront

<first events> then connection closed, later 304 on reconnect
```
Rafi (DevEx): Oof. `etag` + `cache-control` not `no-cache` is a red flag. Some CDNs will respond with 304 on range/conditional requests and close the connection. SSE must not be cached. Also `content-encoding: gzip` can cause buffering in proxies which prevents chunked flush. Safari's EventSource is sensitive: if the connection gets a 304 or the CDN returns an intermediate cache response, Safari often treats that as a terminal condition. Polyfills that rely on XHR streaming may behave differently; older Safari lacks streaming `fetch` but its native EventSource should work if headers are correct.
Jun (Backend): Agreed. Quick checklist for streaming origins behind CDNs:
- Ensure origin returns `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform` and no `etag`/`last-modified` for SSE endpoints.
- Disable gzip/ Brotli on SSE response or use `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` with `Content-Encoding: identity` so intermediaries don't buffer.
- Add `Surrogate-Control: no-store` or Cloudflare `cache-control: no-cache, no-transform` override rules.
- Send periodic keep-alive comments and `:\n` lines and call `res.flush()` after each event.
- Include `retry: 2000` in stream for client reconnect guidance.
Ivy (Client Success): Customer also mentioned they use a polyfill (event-source-polyfill) because some of their users are on older Safari iOS webviews. Could the polyfill be causing the partial output behavior?
Rafi (DevEx): Possibly. Polyfills often emulate EventSource via XHR streaming or chunked responses. If the CDN buffers due to compression or `content-length`, the XHR-based polyfill won't see chunks until the buffer is flushed or the stream closes. Native EventSource in Safari reads as data arrives unless CDN/ proxy buffers. So if they have `content-encoding: gzip` or CloudFront's `compress` enabled, it can break both native and polyfill differently.
Jun (Backend): Repro steps we should ask customer to try:
1) Bypass CDN (point to origin or use a staging hostname) to confirm CDN is the culprit.
2) Ensure origin SSE handler sends headers:
```
res.setHeader('Content-Type','text/event-stream; charset=utf-8');
res.setHeader('Cache-Control','no-cache, no-transform');
res.setHeader('Connection','keep-alive');
// avoid setting ETag / Content-Length
```
and call `res.flush()` after each `res.write("data: ...\n\n")`.
3) Disable compression for that path in the CDN / origin (CloudFront: compress=false or add a behavior returning raw stream).
4) Purge CDN cache and retry.
Tess (Support): I pushed those to the customer. They responded: bypassing CDN solves it — native EventSource on Safari works fine. When behind CloudFront and a Lambda@Edge that adds headers, they see the partials then 304. They can also reproduce by toggling compression.
Rafi (DevEx): That nails it. Actionable fixes:
- Jun: Update streaming endpoint to explicitly disable ETag and Content-Length and set `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform`.
- Ops: Add CloudFront behavior: for `/v1/streams/*` forward all headers, disable caching, set `Compress: false`, and remove `ETag` during origin response.
- Docs: I'll add a streaming troubleshooting guide that covers browser polyfills, Safari quirks, and CDN rules with code snippets and a checklist.
Jun (Backend): I'll prepare a small middleware patch for our express/golang handlers to force SSE-safe headers and ensure we call `flush`. Example Node snippet included for support docs:
```
app.get('/v1/streams/:id', (req,res) => {
  res.setHeader('Content-Type','text/event-stream; charset=utf-8');
  res.setHeader('Cache-Control','no-cache, no-transform');
  res.setHeader('Connection','keep-alive');
  // prevent proxies from adding ETag or content-length
  res.removeHeader('ETag');
  // send first comment
  res.write(': connected\n\n');
  // example event
  res.write('data: {"status":"ok"}\n\n');
  res.flush && res.flush();
});
```
Ivy (Client Success): Customer asked for a minimal client-side workaround while they fix CDN: would adding `cache-control: no-cache` via ajax be possible? They can't control CDN rules immediately.
Rafi (DevEx): On the client side there's little to do. For polyfills, make sure the XHR fallback sets `responseType = 'text'` and parses incremental chunks; but if the CDN buffers, client can't force the CDN. A short-term mitigation: reduce reliance on EventSource and provide a websocket or polling fallback for Safari users behind that CDN. Also adding server-sent `retry: 5000` helps.
Tess (Support): Customer confirmed will schedule a change to CloudFront behavior. They asked for a short troubleshooting note they can hand to their infra team — I'll attach our recommended headers + CloudFront behavior example.
Jun (Backend): I'll create a PR to add middleware + a unit test that ensures SSE routes don't emit `ETag` and that `Content-Encoding` isn't applied. Will tag @Rafi for docs.
Rafi (DevEx): I'll draft the troubleshooting note and include a quick checklist:
- Confirm origin sends `text/event-stream`
- No `ETag`/`Last-Modified`
- `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform`
- Disable compression for SSE paths
- Purge CDN cache after changes
- If using polyfills, verify streaming XHR support or use websocket fallback
I'll post the doc link here when ready.
Tess (Support): Marking as customer-working-on-change. I'll follow up in 48h. Thanks all :heart:

Tess (Support): Closing triage — re-open if customer still sees disconnects after CDN change.
